A 70-year-old Japanese man presented with dysphagia
cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge
Enterobacter cloacae was cultured from the wound
lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss

concepts.why: The patient was diagnosed with T3N0M0 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
Enterobacter cloacae was cultured from the wound.
The patient had a refractory anastomotic fistula.
The patient developed worsening low back pain and fever, and MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrated decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5.
The patient had a history of radiotherapy for laryngeal cancer.
The patient had type 2 diabetes mellitus with an HbA1c of 6.6%.
The patient developed cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge.

rationales.F03: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is directly mentioned in the fact.
rationales.F04: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is mentioned as part of the patient's medical history.
rationales.F06: Radiotherapy for laryngeal cancer indicates a history of laryngeal cancer.
rationales.F07: Cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge suggests a postoperative wound infection.
rationales.F09: Enterobacter cloacae was cultured from the wound, indicating an infection.
rationales.F10: Worsening low back pain could be indicative of spondylodiscitis or spinal osteomyelitis.
rationales.F11: Fever can be associated with infections such as Enterobacter cloacae infection or postoperative wound infection.
rationales.F12: Lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss are symptoms that could suggest spondylodiscitis or spinal osteomyelitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's worsening low back pain, lumbar spinal tenderness, bilateral leg weakness, and MRI findings of decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5, along with Enterobacter cloacae cultured from the blood, support the diagnosis of Spondylodiscitis.
